findings.text: The first paragraph says clearly what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. A newcomer can answer "what is this" within seconds.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: The title is about firstmate, a different project, so a visitor to Athena's home page first wonders whether they are on the right page. Only the second and third paragraphs explain that this page is a sample study made by Athena.

The one section that could show Athena's main promise (traceable models, verdict and cost) is an error message, and it sits right after the header. A newcomer sees the pitch fail before seeing it work, and this hurts trust.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The header has a link meant for the site's owner. A newcomer may think they are expected to make decisions, which is confusing.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The page gives a concrete path to try Athena: prerequisites, clone, install, and a first command that says it runs on the current repository after you press Enter. It does not say whether an API key or paid account is needed, which OS is supported, or whether the Rust toolchain must be installed first. The list asks for a C linker "which cargo needs" but does not list cargo.
findings.source: Next steps: prerequisites list, "./setup.sh", "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The core track opens with firstmate jargon (captain, yolo, in scope, local-only landing). Some entries are defined only by saying the source does not define them. A reader who came to learn about Athena gets a dense look inside another tool's internals.
findings.source: Start here > Words used first: "in scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: Saying "not defined" plainly is honest and shows Athena's traceable-claims discipline. But so many of these entries make the study less useful as an explanation.
findings.source: Glossary entries for "captain call", "durable record", "endpoint", "heartbeat", "wake": "The firstmate source does not define ..."

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to exact file lines at a pinned commit. This shows the traceability Athena promises, and a careful newcomer can check it.
findings.source: Claims and sources: links such as "bin/fm-spawn.sh:194-197" pinned to commit 6407052f…

findings.text: The core/expert toggle hides the Counters and Transitions sections by default. This makes the page shorter for a newcomer, but the default view is still long.
findings.source: Learning path: "Show expert detail (core track is the default)"
